title: The Second Bell
parent_tip: Pick one strong word. What does it hint that a plain one can't?

items.ask: Why does the author open in the wings and then jump back eight months?
choices: to show the recital matters less than her brother's complaints
to explain how the auditorium was built
to build tension before showing what the moment cost her
to prove that Priya never practiced the hard section

items.ask: Which sentence best shows the story returning from the past to the present?
choices: Eight months earlier, she had nearly quit.
Now, in the dim wings, that memory seemed impossibly distant
In March, the measures finally untangled.

items.ask: How does the flashback change the way we read the recital at the end? Use a quote.

answer_key: 1. C (to build tension before showing what the moment cost her)
2. C (Now, in the dim wings, that memory seemed impossibly distant)

3. Sample: The flashback turns the recital into the end of a long struggle instead of a single performance. Because we know she "repeated the same twelve measures" night after night, the moment they "passed in a few seconds" feels like a victory. Without the flashback, those seconds would seem ordinary. Full answer: a claim about the effect, an exact quote from the flashback or the recital, and why it changes the ending
